_doc: Ledger of cartoon shorts (the daily automatic method). The producer appends one entry with status 'produced'; the publish job turns it into 'published'. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a topic listed here.

episodes.title: What If You Jumped Into a Hole Through the Earth?
episodes.topic: falling through a tunnel through the centre of the Earth (gravity tunnel, 38 minutes one way, oscillates forever)

episodes.title: What If You Had to Eat Like a Hummingbird? 🍔
episodes.topic: a man with a hummingbird's energy use per gram: 120,000 calories a day, a burger every three minutes, and too little skin to lose 6 kW of heat (square-cube law); the bird's own answer is nightly torpor
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: the week's top 'what if' row is 'What If Humans Had Hummingbird Hearts' (3.95M views/day) plus an Arabic remake; body and everyday scenarios beat space topics
episodes.note: uploaded private from the rehearsal session, published by the owner; retitled 2026-11-15 from "What If You Had a Hummingbird's Metabolism? 🤔" (plain title test)

episodes.title: What If You Tried to Open a Plane Door Mid-Flight? ✈️
episodes.topic: trying to open an airliner's exit door at cruise: cabin pressure holds the plug door shut with almost 20,000 pounds (8 psi on 2,448 square inches, four cars); suction-cup analogy; it only lets go on the ground
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: 'What if a Plane Door Opened Mid-flight' (2.11M views/day) is the strongest undone 'what if' row; everyday travel scenarios win for several channels this week

episodes.title: What If You Ran in Cinderella's Glass Slippers? 👠
episodes.topic: running in glass slippers: squeezed glass holds about 1000 MPa (a 1 cm cube carries ten tons, two elephants), stretched glass about 40 MPa, twenty-five times less, because of microscopic surface scratches; a running step bends the heel and it snaps; bag-of-chips notch analogy
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: the Cinderella's-slipper question wins for three channels this week (lilBrain 1.76M views/day, Den TV 0.81M, HawdAlafkar 0.61M); we take the theme and ask the physical question

episodes.title: What If the Elevator Cable Snapped? 😱
episodes.topic: every rope of an elevator snaps at once: each of the six ropes could carry the loaded car alone (factor of safety 10.25), and if all part, the overspeed governor trips wedge brakes on the guide rails; the car falls about five feet (3.4 to 7.3 ft) in about a second; a last-second jump takes off at 6 mph against 76 mph; seat-belt analogy; the brakes only release when the car is lifted
episodes.trend: topic_bank: elevator-cable-snaps (44 elevator shorts, 60M views, 43 channels; 'cable snaps' videos reach 27k to 178k views on channels with 50 to 1,250 subscribers); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not already made

episodes.title: What If an Immortal Snail Was Chasing You? 🐌
episodes.topic: a snail that cannot die follows you forever: at the pace of the fastest snail ever timed (13 inches in 2 minutes) and never stopping it does 87 yards a night, 260 yards a day, 54 miles a year; one step is a four-minute lead, a three-minute walk wins a day back, a flight across the Atlantic 64 years; dripping-tap analogy; snails hitch rides on luggage
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: 'Would you take a billion dollars if you were followed by an Immortal Snail forever?' (53.9k-subscriber channel, 1.36M views/day), the week's best real 'what if you' row from a small channel; also topic_bank: immortal-snail (6.7M views on a 5.5k-subscriber channel)

episodes.title: What If You Jumped on a Cloud? ☁️
episodes.topic: jumping onto a small fair-weather cloud from a balloon: it holds 500 tons of water (1.1 million pounds, a hundred elephants) at 0.5 g per cubic metre, so a fridge-sized piece holds ten drops; you fall through a kilometre of it in 22 seconds and meet one cup of water; droplets sink half an inch a second, fog is a cloud that sat down; a million droplets make one raindrop
episodes.trend: topic_bank: jump-on-a-cloud ('what would happen if you jumped on top of a cloud' 927k views on a 6.3k-subscriber channel); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not an advert or already made

episodes.title: What If Friction Vanished for 5 Seconds? 😱
episodes.topic: friction between solid surfaces switches off for five seconds in Gus's garden: feet cannot push, a cup slips through closed fingers, a leaning ladder slides flat, and because a lawn falls 6 inches in 10 feet (building code, so rain runs off) everything on it, heavy or light, slides 20 feet in 5 seconds and ends at a jogging pace, pulled by 9 pounds on a 180-pound man; two-brushes analogy; when grip returns his feet stop and the rest of him keeps going
episodes.trend: topic_bank: friction-off-5-seconds (2.7M views on a 1,640-subscriber channel, the biggest outlier of the sample); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not an advert, a game or a thing a child could copy

episodes.title: What If Lightning Hit Your Plane? ⚡
episodes.topic: lightning strikes the airliner Gus is asleep on: a typical bolt (30,000 A, five times hotter than the sun's surface) is 2,000 times the current that blows a kitchen fuse, yet it runs through the aluminium skin (thinner than a dime) from nose to tail, which takes only a few volts (Ohm's law: about 6 V, less than a wall socket); every airliner is hit about once a year and nine times out of ten sets the bolt off itself; umbrella analogy; the dry cabin, the carpet and his slippers then give him a 3,000-volt doorknob spark
episodes.trend: topic_bank: lightning-hits-your-plane (129k views on a 686-subscriber channel; the plane cluster: 60 videos, 171M views, 43 channels); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not an advert, a game or already made

episodes.title: What If a Fart Was Your Only Rocket in Space? 🚀
episodes.topic: Gus is stranded ten feet from his ship and tries a fart as a rocket: a tenth of a gram of gas at ten feet a second moves 460 pounds (man plus suit) one hair's width a minute, so ten feet takes over three weeks against eight hours of air; a rocket moves by throwing mass away, what counts is how much and how fast (skateboard and backpack analogy); a half-pound slipper thrown at 20 mph is six thousand times the push and takes him home in five minutes; and a spacesuit is airtight, so the fart never left the helmet
episodes.trend: topic_bank: fart-rocket-in-space ('What if You Fart in Space' 57M and 'Fart In A Space Suit' 25M on giant channels; 'If You Fart in a Silent Elevator' 3.4M on an 18.7k-subscriber channel); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not an advert, a game or already made

episodes.title: What If Gravity Switched Off for 5 Seconds? 😱
episodes.topic: gravity lets go of Gus's garden for five seconds: whatever sits still stays put (at 40 N the spinning ground, 800 mph, only sinks 10 inches from under his wife's chair), but anything already moving keeps its speed (Newton's first law), so a pancake flipped at 8 feet a second never comes back and a one-foot hop carries Gus 32 feet up in 4 seconds with the pancake 8 feet out of reach; gravity is a brake (ball up a hill against ball on a flat floor); when it returns he coasts one more foot to 33 feet, the height of the 10 m Olympic diving platform, and hits the neighbor's pool at 30 mph; the pancake lands on him
episodes.trend: topic_bank: gravity-off-5-seconds (the 'for 5 seconds' family: 13 videos, 46M views, 31M of them on channels under 100k subscribers); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not an advert, a game, a film or already made

episodes.title: What If Both Engines Quit on Your Plane? ✈️
episodes.topic: both engines of an airliner stop at 38,000 ft: it glides about fifteen miles for each mile it sinks (flatter than a wheelchair ramp), over a hundred miles in almost twenty minutes; bike coasting downhill analogy; the 2001 glide of 75 miles to an island; ram air turbine; a normal descent is at idle from a hundred miles out
episodes.trend: topic bank (plane cluster) in Thanksgiving travel week: google_trends 'radar' with the O'Hare ground stop on the busiest travel day; no fresh everyday what-if row in youtube_shorts (adverts and GTA 6)

episodes.title: What If Your Pool Was 100 Feet Deep? 😱
episodes.topic: Gus digs a back-garden pool a hundred feet deep (190 dump trucks of dirt, 24 days of garden hose) and lowers a beach ball to the bottom on a barbell: 34 feet of fresh water weigh as much as the whole atmosphere, so at 100 feet there are four atmospheres, the ball is squeezed to a quarter of its volume (the size of a basketball, Boyle's law) and every square foot of floor holds up three tons of water; bottom-pancake-of-the-stack analogy; pulled up, the ball grows back; Gus cannot swim and keeps to the top two feet
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: 'What If You Dug a 60-Foot Pool in Your Backyard?' (111k-subscriber channel, 4.11M views/day) is the week's strongest real 'what if' row, and the backyard-digging theme also pulls for a 1,500-subscriber channel (295k views/day); we take the theme and ask what the bottom is like
